articleTitle: Investigation of grinding performance in ultrasonic vibration assisted grinding of Ti-6Al-4 V alloy using minimum quantity lubrication
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Minimum quantity lubrication (MQL) is an efficient cooling and lubrication technique usually used these days in grinding operation. It is found to be advantageous for improving the grinding performance in terms of reduced grinding forces, surface integrity and production cost since it offers better cooling, lubrication, and lower coolant consumption. Ultrasonic vibration assisted grinding (UAG) has also shown the improvement in the grinding performance owing to the change in the nature of cutting process in UAG. In this study, the grinding performance of UAG combined with MQL using soluble oil on Ti-6Al-4V alloy is studied through surface grinding experiments. The results show significant improvement in surface finish and reduction in grinding forces are achieved in UAG with MQL grinding process as compared with conventional dry and ultrasonic vibration assisted dry grinding.

articleTitle: A Computationally Efficient Machine Learning Strategy for Automatic Identification of Process and Product Fingerprints for Smart Manufacturing Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: The process/product fingerprints framework strategy has been developed to reduce the number of process/product characterisation parameters and establish the functional relationship among them. Recently this strategy was developed using machine learning as it automatically identifies them and minimizes the influence of human decisions. However, the previously developed framework can't be tested for each fingerprint candidate since it requires a lot of computational time for model training and evaluation. Since all combinations can't be considered, accuracy may affect a lot. Hence this study presented a computationally efficient machine learning framework for fingerprints development. Data obtained from a nanosecond pulsed laser ablation process has been used to validate the performance of the proposed framework. The results show that the proposed framework is at least seven times faster than the previously developed framework using the given data set.

articleTitle: A preliminary study of micro thin wall fabrication on PMMA using an in-house developed micromilling machine
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Micromilling has been increasingly employed for fabrication of micro geometrical features in many miniature parts, but the machining of micro thin walls is considered as difficult due to low material rigidity, and easy deformation by cutting force. In this study, a low-cost and reconfigurable 3-axis micromilling machine was developed by integrating a XYZ precision motion stage with a high-speed spindle. The development and configuration of the micromilling platform is introduced, along with a calibration of the motion accuracy and a vision-assisted tool tip positioning approach. Preliminary experimental study was conducted to fabricate micro thin walls on PMMA workpiece under different conditions. While the thin walls with a target thickness of 300 μm were successfully machined, it was found that there were many issues encountered in the machining of the 30 μm thin walls. The defects were analyzed to identify the root-causes and future research directions.

articleTitle: Development of a wafer-level dicing system with controllable pulse femtosecond laser
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: The cutting of hard-brittle transparent materials is widely used in chip manufacturing, optical manufacturing and many other fields. In order to realize the high-quality wafer-level cutting process of composite glass, a wafer-level dicing system with controllable pulse femtosecond laser is developed in this paper. The system achieves complete control over the pulse in time and space. With the processing advantages of the femtosecond laser Bessel beam, the synchronized time and synchronized position can be flexibly adjusted to achieve better processing results. Through experimental verification and theoretical analysis, the effects of Time Synchronization Output(TSO) and Position Synchronization Output(PSO) on the roughness of the cut samples are studied, and the minimum roughness 800 nm of the cross-section is obtained on the composite borosilicate glass. The results show that the controllable pulse can effectively optimize the cutting process to obtain less roughness and shape error. Controllable pulse cutting expands the processing application range of femtosecond laser Bessel beams, and can derive more cutting processes.

articleTitle: Test of a novel microlens grating based miniature spectrometers array for chromatic confocal technology
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Multifocal chromatic confocal techniques have important applications in 3D measurement. A chromatic confocal system consists of a dispersive objective, a light source, a fiber coupler, and a spectrometer. An array of spectrometers is required when applying a chromatic confocal sensor for multifocal scanning. A novel microspectrometer array utilizing a single hybrid optical device with microlens array and grating surface on its two sides is developed, which differs from the state-of-the-art micro or miniature spectrometers array usually with a combination use of a microlens arrays a grating. For investigation of feasibility of these microlens array-grating based microspectrometer in multifocal chromatic confocal scanning, we built a chromatic confocal system and test bench, developed an evaluation methodology. Testing results demonstrated that the repeatability of detection is in 0.5 pixel. which proves that the microlens grating spectrometer is reliable.

articleTitle: Research on chemical mechanical polishing of KTiOPO4crystal
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: With the development of laser equipment industry, higher requirements were put forward for the surface quality of <tex>$\boldsymbol{KTiOPO_{4}}$</tex> (KTP). With SiO<inf>2</inf> abrasive, oxidant hydrogen peroxide, pH value regulator KOH and citric acid, chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) of KTP crystal was carried out, and the surface roughness was taken as the assessment indicator. The components of the polishing slurry were optimized in the research process. Provided that diameter of <tex>$\boldsymbol{SiO_{2}}$</tex> is 20 nm, mass fraction of <tex>$\boldsymbol{SiO_{2}}$</tex> is 10 %, pH value is 10 and <tex>$\boldsymbol{H_{2}O_{2}}$</tex> is 3 wt%, the ultra-smooth crystal surface (less than 0.2 nm) with good uniformity is obtained.

articleTitle: Theoretical Analysis on Gauge Block Length Measurement by Excess Fraction method
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: The method of Excess Fraction (EF) has been widely employed to determine the integer fringe order in interferometric metrology. In this paper, we describe the principle of EF method which selects the optimum difference cj between the real length and nominal length. Besides, theoretical analysis and numerical simulation based on the experimental data of employed wavelengths and corresponding excess fraction values from three different wavelength groups have been implemented to illustrate the influence of experimental errors on the final result.

articleTitle: Interferometer for multi-degree-of-freedom measurement using ball lens and liquid crystal
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: In this research, by using the principle of transmissive liquid crystals in interferometry, simultaneous measurement of multi-degree-of-freedom (DOF) motion is realized in a single measurement system. Therefore, by using it in combination with a polarizer to arbitrarily switch the light path of the interferometer between transmission and block during measurement, it is possible to perform multiple motion measurements simultaneously. In this research, multiple ball lenses (BL) are used as target mirrors, and since BLs have the property of retroreflecting incident light, light enters the photodetector if the laser beam enters the BLs, regardless of the movement of the target. By switching between light transmission and block, multi-degree-of-freedom measurement becomes possible. In this paper, one-DOF measurement of horizontal translational motion perpendicular to the optical axis direction was performed.

articleTitle: Theoretical investigation of angle measurement based on third-harmonic generation (THG) with a femtosecond laser
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed the concept of angle measurement based on third-harmonic generation (THG), which can be produced in a wider range of materials than the second harmonic generation (SHG). The theoretical investigation has been done by considering the direct third harmonic generation process, and three typical nonlinear crystals, including BBO, LiIO<inf>3,</inf> and KDP are used for the sensitivity analysis. The analysis shows the angle dependence of the THG has the sinc function form, which means the maximum intensity can occur around the phase-matching angle. Based on this, the simulation investigation was done nearing the phase-matching angle, and the calculation results indicate that the BBO crystal has the best angular measurement sensitivity because of the low dispersion and the fast peak shift in the investigated spectral range compared with the other two crystals.

articleTitle: Spiral Compensation of Surface Error in Ultra-Precision Micro-milling of Spherical Micro Lens Array with a tilt spindle
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Micro Lens Arrays (MLA) with aspherical or spherical elements, have been widely used in opto-electro industries, such as sensor devices, optical communication, beam shaping etc. MLA can be fabricated efficiently by low-cost replication of micro lenses through injection molding. In order to meet the optical properties of MLA, profile accuracy and surface roughness of molds are usually in the sub-micron level and the nanometer level. To improve the machining accuracy and consistency of MLA, high-speed micro-milling was selected for machining of MLA. An error model of radius of gyration and 3D spiral compensation approach was developed for the micro-milling of MLA molds with a tilt spindle rather than a vertical spindle. The overall surface error after milling was obtained and was then used to generate a new spiral tool path for compensation milling. The experimental results showed that the surface form accuracy decreased from 5.2 μm to 0.6 μm (in PV) after two compensation milling cycles. This demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed surface error compensation methods for the spiral micro-milling of MLA molds.

articleTitle: High-precision phase extraction and unwrapping method for MEMS mirror structured light system
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Phase extraction and unwrapping is an important part of structured light three-dimensional (3D) measurement. High-precision phase extraction and unwrapping methods are of great significance for realizing high-precision structured light 3D measurement. In this paper, the following researches are made on the phase extraction and unwrapping method in the structured light 3D measurement system based on micro-electromechanical system (MEMS) mirror. This paper adopts the standard N-step phase-shift method to extract phase. Considering the measurement time and measurement accuracy, the four-step phase-shift method is finally selected after the phase error experiment and analysis. The phase unwrapping algorithm selects the multi-frequency step-by-step unwrapping method which is not sensitive to the phase error. For the nonlinear error of the system, phase error compensation based on Hilbert transform is carried out, and the phase error after compensation is reduced by 64.5% compared with that before compensation. Finally, a three-dimensional reconstruction experiment was carried out using the above method and a structured light three-dimensional measurement system based on MEMS mirror. The experimental results show that the measured objects have been effectively 3D reconstructed.

articleTitle: Shaping of micro mould tools manufactured by UV LIGA and Selective Laser Melting (SLM)
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Polymeric micro and nano surface structures are used widely in microfluidics, micro-optics and functional surfaces. Replication processes for these structures, e.g. micro injection moulding, hot embossing, are critical, but constricted by demoulding. Demoulding defects caused by friction, adhesion and thermal stresses, can cause microstructure distortion or, damage, and thus influence the final product performance. Forming and shaping of micro-tools will facilitate demoulding. In this research, two fabrication processes i.e., UV LIGA and SLM have been used to manufacture micro moulds of Ni and 316L SS. A highly precise process, UV LIGA, is used to make micro features of nickel having a low surface roughness Sa (<50nm). A faster but less precise microfabrication process is also used, SLM 3D printing, to manufacture stainless steel micro features having a high surface roughness Sa (>1μm). Moulds manufactured using these two processes are subjected to electropolishing to examine changes in geometry and surface roughness. Electropolishing is used for shaping and polishing of the micro features to bring a design change and address demoulding challenges. To ensure a green environment and human safety, nickel sulfamate solution is also used for electropolishing. EP has the potential to shape and polish micro features, thus enhancing mould release performance.

articleTitle: Effect of cutting direction on nanomachining of copper when using a three-sided pyramidal AFM tip
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: In this paper, a three-sided pyramidal AFM tip was used to machine copper using both face forward and edge forward directions. Different process outcomes are expected due to such directional variations. However, this paper aims further to quantify such changes, including differences in groove depths, pile-up heights, and surface roughness, as well as with respect to groove formation mechanisms and relative stability of the process. To achieve this, the study also includes analyzing data recorded during nanomachining via the built-in position-sensitive photo-detector of AFM instruments. Such data correspond to lateral and torsional deflections of the cantilever on which the AFM tip is mounted. The experiments confirmed that significant changes in groove pile-ups, depths, and widths took place when these two cutting directions were analyzed. Additionally, cutting via chip formation was observed in the face forward direction, whereas only ploughing was seen in the edge forward direction. Conversely, no considerable difference between the surface roughness along each groove length for each of these directions was found. Finally, substantial contrast between the two directions was noticed when analyzing the data acquisition output. In particular, the induced vertical and torsional motions of the cantilever were generally more stable along the edge forward direction.

articleTitle: Experimental study on efficient micro-milling of Alumina with PCD and cBN micro-milling tools
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Currently, micro-milling of very hard and brittle materials such as ceramics is relatively unfeasible due to significant tool wear, tool breakage and poor surface quality during machining. In this article, single straight edge cubic boron nitride (cBN) and double straight edge polycrystalline diamond (PCD) micro-milling tools were manufactured, and a systematic experimental study was conducted on micro-milling of pure alumina (Al<inf>2</inf>O<inf>3</inf>) workpiece in order to achieve effective and efficient machining. The influence of cutting parameters, namely feed per tooth (fz), tool material and workpiece material, are investigated in relation to the cutting force, achievable surface roughness and tool wear. Identified modes of tool wear are observed. Further tests were also conducted in order to achieve large depth of cut on alumina toughened zirconia ATZ. The results show that both tool materials are suitable for micro-milling of very hard and brittle ceramic materials. However, the double straight edge (DSEE) PCD micro-milling tool provided lower and more stable cutting forces than the single straight edge (SSEE) cBN micro-milling tool, as well as better surface quality in relation to surface roughness. The PCD tools also maintained excellent structural integrity and only minor tool wear during micro-milling of both workpiece materials. Finally, successful micro-milling with a large depth of cut of 120 um of pure alumina was achieved.

articleTitle: A study on the electrochemical oxidation assisted ultra-precision machining of Tungsten Carbide superalloy
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Tungsten carbide (WC) superalloy has been widely used as an excellent mold material for its high hardness, good wear resistance and corrosion resistance. However, the high hardness leads to the difficulty of optically qualified complex surfaces machining. Ultra-precision machining (UPM) technique utilizes crystalline diamond as a cutting tool, which enables the generation of optical surface in nanometer scale. Despite this, diamond cutting tool suffers both mechanical wear and chemical wear when cutting WC. In this study, an integrated method combining electrochemical oxidation and diamond cutting has been proposed. It is demonstrated that surface modification by electrochemical oxidation can drastically reduce the tool wear of the diamond tool. To improve the machining performance and its overall efficiency, the underlying mechanism based on the surface microstructures during the electrochemical assisted process has been analyzed in detail. The surface morphology and surface composition were investigated after the electrochemical exposure under various voltage and current parameters. The results present that a uniform oxide layer up to 15.89 μm can be formed. It is found the Cobalt (Co) phase has the priority to oxidize. As the reaction proceeds, WC phase is also oxidized emitting CO<inf>2</inf> gas, making the oxide layer loose. Despite this, the surface is modified and thus the hardness of the target area can be reduced effectively, which increase diamond tool life during machining.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Classification and Analysis of Wire-EDM Discharge Pulses
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Wire electrical discharge machining (wire-EDM) process is having immense potential over conventional machining methods due to its non-contact nature of material removal. However, frequent and unanticipated machining failures like wire breakages negatively affect the productivity, sustainability and efficiency of the process. In this context, there is a wide scope to improve the process efficiency through online condition monitoring. A prominent aspect of EDM condition monitoring is discharge pulse discrimination. The threshold based methods which are currently being used has low accuracy and is reliant on operator's experience. In this study, a machine learning (ML) based pulse classification based on the extracted discharge characteristics is proposed. The features are extracted from the raw voltage and current senor signals collected from the machining zone during the wire EDM operation. Among the various ML models, Artificial Neural Network (ANN) classifier is found to have the maximum prediction accuracy of 98 %. Also, the effects of different discharge pulses on the productivity, surface finish and machining failures are investigated. The short circuit and arc discharges are found to cause wire breakage failure if they predominate the pulse cycle by more than 80 %. Also, short and arc sparks increase the surface roughness significantly, by up to 70 %.

articleTitle: Laser-based surface modification assisted ultra-precision machining of polycrystalline tin
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Laser surface modification can improve the processing performance of soft metal materials. In this work, a laser-based surface modification assisted ultra-precision machining method is proposed. A continuous wave fiber laser with a wavelength of 1064 nm is used to achieve surface modification. Based on the self-built laser modification device, the surface modification experiments of polycrystalline tin under different laser power densities were carried out. The depth of the modified layer under different power densities was analyzed, and single-point diamond turning experiments were carried out. The results show that the machined surface roughness obtained by ultra-precision cutting experiments in the modified layer is much lower than that of the unmodified surface. In addition, the causes of surface ablation pools and scratches under high laser power densities are analyzed.

articleTitle: Theoretical Modelling of Subsurface Damage in Ultra-Precision Grinding of Fused Silica
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Fused silica is a typically brittle material with high hardness and low fracture toughness. Ultra-precision grinding technology is an effective method to improve the machinability of fused silica with high surface quality. To achieve low damage grinding of fused silica, the grinding performance with different grinding parameters was investigated and the material removal mode was also presented after determining the critical cutting depth. The subsurface microcrack was analyzed using indentation fracture mechanics, and a mathematical relationship model between the subsurface damage depth <tex>$\boldsymbol{h_{SSD}}$</tex> and the maximum height of surface roughness <tex>$\boldsymbol{S_{z}}$</tex> was established. The relatively optimum surface quality of <tex>$\boldsymbol{S_{z}=1.986\mu \mathrm{m}}$</tex> and subsurface damage depth <tex>$\boldsymbol{h_{SSD}=2.65\mu \mathrm{m}}$</tex> was achieved. The theoretical values of the established model were found to agree well with the actual measured values, which indicates that the model can be used for non-destructive detection of subsurface damage depth.

articleTitle: Investigation of the material removal process in fluid line-jet polishing by CFD simulation
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Fluid jet polishing has been extensively utilized in the ultra-precision manufacturing of optical components and molds. Different shapes of nozzles are designed to improve the polishing performance. Among them, the nozzle with a line shape can enhance the polishing efficiency greatly and has the potential to obtain better performance in uniform polishing. However, our scientific understanding of the material removal process in fluid line-jet polishing (FLJP) is far from complete at present, which makes it difficult to predict the surface generation and optimize the polishing process. In this paper, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation was conducted to characterize the material removal process and model the tool influence function in FLJP. The abrasive impact information, fluid flow field, and abrasive trajectory were also analyzed. The study can not only provide a better understanding of the material removal characteristics but also provide theoretical basis for the prediction of surface generation in FLJP.

articleTitle: Research on surface generation in the ultra-precision parallel grinding of curved surfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Ultra-precision parallel grinding has been widely used in the fabrication of various complex curved surfaces for the advanced optical components with high precision and smoothness. In comparison with the machining of flat and spheric surfaces, in grinding of the curved surfaces, the concavity-convexity and local curvature of the workpiece change continuously along the wheel path, which imposes nonuniform scallop height generation. In this paper, three types of sinusoidal wave surface were ground and the influence of curvature on scallop height generation was studied. It is found that the scallop height has a close relationship with the curvature feature of the workpiece and the scallop height is relatively small in the area with relatively gentle curvature, however, for the area with larger curvature, the scallop height of the machined surface increased both for concave and convex surface regions, especially for the concave area, which further increases the scallop height of sine profile. The results show that changes in curvature can significantly cause uneven scallop height distribution for the grinding of curved surfaces due to the different wheel-location points between two adjacent tool loci at the same angular position in ultra-precision parallel grinding.

articleTitle: Investigation of field-amplified sample stacking in microchannels
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Herein, concentration enrichment of sample solutes is obtained by using field-amplified sample stacking (FASS) in microchannel. Numerical investigations are performed to explored the effects of different parameters including the applied voltage, the charged properties of the sample, the buffer concentration ratio, and the injection length on the enrichment performance, and to study the influence of Joule heating effect on FASS. Furthermore, a high conductance gradient boundary is established by photoinitiating fabrication of a porous plug at the enriched interface position. Experimental results show that the fluorescein-Na with 0.1 μM initial concentrations achieves a 329-fold enrichment.

articleTitle: Atomic-scale and Damage-free Smoothing of $\boldsymbol{\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}}$ via Plasma-induced Atom Migration Manufacturing (PAMM)
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: <tex>$\boldsymbol{\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}}$</tex> is an emerging next-generation ultra-wide bandgap semiconductor that shows great application potentials in high-power, high-frequency, and high-temperature electronic devices. However, its atomic-scale smoothing is a troublesome issue due to the natural difficult-to-machine feature. Herein, we proposed a damage-free technique to achieve the atomic-scale smoothing of <tex>$\boldsymbol{\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}}$</tex> using atmospheric pressure inductively coupled plasma (ICP). It is found that the high-temperature pure Ar ICP can impel surface atoms to migrate on <tex>$\boldsymbol{\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}}$</tex>, thus leading to the formation of atomically smooth surface following the decrease of surface energy, which is called plasma-induced atom migration manufacturing (PAMM). After the treatment at 900 W for 40 min, the Sa surface roughness dramatically decreases from 15.3 nm to 0.43 nm, and atomic-scale step-terrace structures can be observed on the atomically smooth substrate. Additionally, the crystal quality of <tex>$\boldsymbol{\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}}$</tex> after PAMM is found to be greatly improved. We believe this novel PAMM technique can provide new sights into the nanomanufacturing research towards next-generation semiconductors and further promote the development of <tex>$\boldsymbol{\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}}$</tex> -based electronic devices.

articleTitle: Assessment and investigation of SPH modelling for nano-scratching
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: The computational modelling of nano-machining using Smooth Particles Hydrodynamics (SPH) method is a research area of recent interest. Among the papers which focus on SPH simulation of nano-machining on copper workpieces, Johnson-Cook model parameters obtained at macro-scale have been used previously [1]–[3] for describing constitutive properties of copper. This paper establishes a SPH model for nano-scratching on copper workpiece with the aim of evaluating the feasibility of using these macro-scale Johnson-Cook parameters in SPH simulation of nano-scale machining. The geometrical parameters for tool tip and workpiece for SPH modelling of nano-scratching is adopted from Islam et al. [4] and simulation results are compared with the experimental work of these authors which was reported in [4] and [5]. The analysis of machining forces shows that the cutting and normal forces slightly increase as the cutting speed increases, and that these are close to experimental results. Simulation results also show that ploughing is the main mode of surface deformation and that the cross-sectional profile of a machined nano-groove matches well with experimental results. This paper contributes towards further elaborating the suitability of employing macro-scale Johnson-Cook parameters in the SPH simulation of nano-machining to predict material responses.

articleTitle: 3D thermodynamic optimal design of superhydrophobic surfaces using periodic microstructures
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Though many superhydrophobic surfaces have been produced by mimicking biological materials and show great prospects in aerospace, navigation, architecture, and biomedical devices, it is still left uncertain which surficial microstructure is the most optimal to use and the thermodynamic mechanism behind. Many previous works focused on the dependence of surface contact angle and contact angle hysteresis on microstructures via different models. But only a few of them have taken the kink model of the three-phase contact line motion into account. In this work, we consider the kink model of the contact line motion and take a 3D microtextured surface with paraboloid structures as an example to revisit the prediction of surface superhydrophobic properties. The dependence of the superhydrophobicity on the structure shape and different structural parameters are discussed. This work helps reveal structural factors that govern the optimal design of superhydrophobic microstructures, paving the way for high-efficiency production of high-performance films.

articleTitle: Laser processing of NdFeB micro-array structure
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: NdFeB is widely used in micro electromagnetic linear motors because of its excellent magnetic properties, but its hard and brittle characteristics deteriorate its machinability and thus affect its application prospects. Laser processing finds wide application in the field of hard and brittle materials because of its high energy density, small heat affected zone and high processing accuracy. In order to produce high quality micro-array structures on NdFeB surface, this paper investigated the influence of laser parameters on the processing of micro-array structures on NdFeB surface, and seeked the optimal parameters for laser processing. This paper provides useful help for the processing of NdFeB surface microstructures, which can help to improve the performance of the slider in micro linear motor and promote its upgrading.

articleTitle: Surface modification of silicon carbide at atomic and close-to-atomic scale by femtosecond laser
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Hexagonal silicon carbide exhibits great potential in various applications due to the excellent physical and chemical properties. However, the nature of hard and brittle makes it difficult to processing especially at atomic scale. In this study, the irradiation of femtosecond laser pulse on 4H-SiC (0001) Si-face is studied using both the experiments and the simulations of hybrid molecular dynamics (MD) and two temperature model (TTM). The removal and amorphous of material induced by single laser pulse are investigated with different fluences, and the influence of energy absorption depths is discussed. An ablation crater with 4 nm depth and sub-diffraction limited size is detected, implying the importance of multi-photon ionization. This study provides an atomic view on the interaction of laser with silicon carbide, illustrating that pulsed laser with shorter wavelength is more suitable for propelling atomic and close-to-atomic scale manufacturing (ACSM).

articleTitle: Study on the effects of processing parameters on machining outcomes under AFM tip-based nanomilling approach
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: In current ultra-precision machining realm, AFM tip-based nanomachining technique is of highly interest. In this study, AFM tip-based nanomilling is used to fabricate nanochannels with controllable dimension size on PMMA sheet. The channel size was mainly determinated by the driving voltage and frequency of the signal that inputted to the shaking table. Besides, to reveal the details of machining outcomes in nanomilling process, the tip motion trajectory was studied. The effects of machining parameters including machining velocity, driving frequency, rotation amplitude, feed speed and normal load on the machined results were investigated. Results showed that the bottom of the machined channel was flatter than that obtained by conventional scratching. Particularly the machined depth, chip formation and the material accumulation were affected by the machining parameters. The nanochannels fabricated using the optimized nanomilling parameters can be applied in the nanofluidic field.

articleTitle: An improved photometric stereo method for the online defect detection of gearbox covers
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: The defects on the surface of a gearbox cover can affect its high performance and high air-tightness. To ensure its high functionality, it's necessary to detect the surface defects. The photometric stereo (PS) method is widely applied to defect detection in the industry for its high accuracy and high speed. However, the traditional PS simply applies to static scenes. To solve this problem, we proposed an improved photometric stereo method that can detect defects in dynamic scenes with high speed and high accuracy. Experiments are designed to verify the feasibility of our method and the results showed that our method performs well with objects with complex shapes.

articleTitle: Design of a hybrid Total-internal-reflection Collimator
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: A hybrid structural total internal reflection (TIR) collimator is designed based on Snell's law for the secondary light distribution for the projectors. The performance of the system were evaluated through simulation. The illumination uniformity of the system reached over 94% and the luminous flux utilization rate was over 91% based on simulation using by LightTools software. The axial-symmetrical collimating system has various impressive features, for instance, simple and compact structure, small size, lightweight, and high illumination uniformity, which can meet the requirements of the augmented reality (AR) glasses or projectors.

articleTitle: Experiment and simulation study on the demolding process of injection-molded microfluidic chips for heavy metal detection
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: The demolding process of polymer microfluidic chips fabricated by injection molding will directly affect their performance. In this study, experiments and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation were combined to investigate the demolding quality of the microstructures for heavy metal detection on microfluidic chips. The experimental results showed that the microfluidic chips could be completely molded, but the edges of the microstructures were stretched to a certain extent and the bottom of the microchannel was depressed. The simulation results showed that the interfacial adhesion between the polymer molecular chains and the mold insert was the main factor affecting the demolding resistance. Furthermore, the change of the gyration radius was used to characterize the deformations of polymer molecular chains during the demolding process. The MD method can effectively explain the internal mechanisms of interfacial interactions that cause the demolding deformations of polymer structures from the molecular/atomic scale.

articleTitle: Toolpath generation based on innovative rotary coordinate and shuttling element in ultra-precision diamond turning of optical microstructures
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Toolpath generation techniques have become increasingly critical in ultra-precision diamond turning for optical microstructure as the dramatically promoted complexity of structural geometry. However, the spiral toolpath topology is usually difficult to be adapted to the mathematical expression or scattered point clouds with quadrilateral meshing method used for the conventional structure models. In this paper, a creative spiral toolpath generation method integrated geometric modelling for ultra-precision turning is proposed. By the innovative rotary coordinate and shuttling element method, the point clouds for microstructure modelling could be scattered along the spiral topology which can be directly fitted as the final toolpath. According to the simulation experiment, this method can dramatically reduce the operation time of modelling and toolpath generation in diamond turning, and ameliorate the fitting accuracy and feeding motion.

articleTitle: Nanomanipulation of carbon nanotubes using fiber probe-based near-field optical tweezers
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: In recent years, the near-field optical tweezers have gradually attracted more and more attention due to their high accuracy and low impact. This paper presents a new method for manipulating carbon nanotubes using fiber-optic probes to generate near-field optical tweezers based on a Scanning Electron Microscope(SEM). An electric field analysis model of the near-field optical tweezers was constructed, and the model was analyzed using the Finite Difference Time Domain(FDTD) method to simulate the manipulation process of near-field optical tweezers, which verified the feasibility of its basic theory and the near-field optical tweezers' operating ability. The bending deformation of carbon nanotubes was realized by the integration of the near-field enhanced optical tweezers based on SEM. This method of nanomanipulation with near-field enhanced optical tweezers based on SEM has the advantages of real-time operation and non-contact, which will open up new ideas and technologies for subsequent research.

articleTitle: A micro-electroforming simulation model with dynamic diffusion coefficient for predicting void defects in microstructure
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: To help reduce or eliminate the void defects, it is critical to accurately predict the size of void defects prior to electroforming experiments. In this study, the limiting current density of nickel ion inside the microchannels of the cathode with a depth of 60 <tex>$\boldsymbol{\mu\mathrm{m}}$</tex> and a width from 24 to 120 <tex>$\boldsymbol{\mu\mathrm{m}}$</tex> are tested by electrochemical experiments. The diffusion layer thickness is assumed to the microchannel depth, and the measured diffusion coefficient are from <tex>$\boldsymbol{1.27\times 10^{-9}\mathrm{m}^{2}/\mathrm{s}}$</tex> to <tex>$\boldsymbol{4.74\times 10^{-9}\mathrm{m}^{2}/\mathrm{s}}$</tex>, corresponding to the different microchannel with different aspect ratio (2.5:1 to 1:2). The simulation models of dynamic diffusion coefficient and constant diffusion coefficient are established, and the corresponding simulation results are compared with the void defects obtained by micro-electroforming experiments. The results show that when the cathode current densities is 2 A/dm<sup>2</sup> and 4 A/dm<sup>2</sup>, the size of void defects obtained by the dynamic model is closer to the experimental results.

articleTitle: The effects of NaOH anodization on surface properties of a bioresorbable WE43 alloy
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: In this study, the effect of anodization on the WE43 surface was investigated. The primary purpose was to achieve a corrosion-resistant surface that can be firmly bonded to polymers to design bioresorbable drug-eluting stents. WE43 samples were anodized at 4,5,6 volts and at different times after finding the best potential region for anodization. Potentiodynamic polarization showed that the sample anodized at 4 volts and 5 minutes had three times lower corrosion rate than the bare WE43 sample. Also, <tex>$\boldsymbol{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{a}}}$</tex> and Sa values indicated that anodization increases the surface bonding ability. The formation of a thin layer of stearic acid on the surface decreased the hydrophilicity of the anodized WE43 samples leading to better corrosion properties.

articleTitle: Vibration-assisted Force Rheological Polishing
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: The force rheological polishing (FRP) technology is a new non-contact ultra-precision polishing method utilizing the nonlinear rheological properties of non-Newtonian fluid. To further improve the polishing efficiency and surface quality, a vibration-assisted force rheological polishing (VFRP) method is proposed in this research. The material removal rate (MRR) and surface roughness <tex>$\boldsymbol{S}_{\boldsymbol{a}}$</tex> were used as evaluation conditions to analyze the effects of three key parameters, including polishing speed, vibration frequency, and amplitude on the polishing characteristics of stainless steel. The experiment was designed based on the Taguchi method, the S/N was used to evaluate the experimental results and the optimized process parameters were obtained, and the weight of each factor was obtained by variance analysis method. Under the optimized combination of polishing parameters, VFRP can effectively improve the polishing efficiency and workpiece surface quality.

articleTitle: Graphene Photodetector Integrated with Waveguide Bragg Grating
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Graphene is a two-dimensional material with excellent photoelectric properties, but the light absorption efficiency is only 2.3<sup>%</sup>. Waveguide integration is an effective way to improve the optical absorption rate of graphene, but the waveguide structure is still limited by complex process, low absorption efficiency, large loss and other problems. To solve these problems, a graphene photodetector integrated with waveguide Bragg grating is proposed in this paper. Under the premise of ensuring absorption efficiency and convenient preparation, this structure is used to enhance the optical response of graphene in the <tex>$\boldsymbol{1550\text{nm}}$</tex> communication band. In this paper, the parameters of graphene photodetector integrated with waveguide Bragg grating are designed, and the simulation is carried out according to the parameters. Simulation results show that compared with traditional waveguide detectors, the optical absorption of the device is improved by one order of magnitude, and has certain wide-band corresponding characteristics, which greatly improves the optical absorption efficiency of graphene. Therefore, this device will have a very wide application prospect in the field of communication.

articleTitle: Preface
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: The proceedings contain all the papers presented at the 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing (nanoMan2022) and the 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (AETS2022) which were organised by the International Society for Nanomanufacturing (ISNM) and International Academy of Engineering and Technology (AET) and hosted by University College Dublin, Ireland, and with IEEE Photonics Society UK & Ireland Chapter as a technical sponsor.

articleTitle: A Conceptual Framework of Cyber-Physical Remanufacturing System
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Remanufacturing has been regarded as one of the most effective methods for extending the life cycle and saving materials of the End-of-Life (EOL) products. Different from traditional highly integrated and automated manufacturing systems, remanufacturing systems have to manage various uncertain factors and small-batch customized production plans. Currently, the intelligence and autonomy of remanufacturing systems are at the initial stage, which cannot support autonomous decision-makings and optimization of production plans. Inspired by the widespread applications of the Digital Twin (DT) and Cyber-Physical System (CPS) in smart manufacturing, this paper proposes a conceptual framework of Cyber-Physical Remanufacturing System (CPRS) to improve the automation, intelligence and capability of the remanufacturing system. Based on the proposed seven steps of remanufacturing process, the CPRS is represented as a three-layer structure. The physical layer and edge layer are introduced for representing the components of physical entities and DT models in CPRS respectively. The cloud service layer represents the potential applications of CPRS. The interactions among different components and different layers are also introduced. Then, the research challenges of developing the CPRS are identified. Future development trends and research directions for implementing the actual application of CPRS are also discussed in conclusion.

articleTitle: Digital Twin Technology for CNC Machining: A Review
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Digital twin technologies have witnessed widespread development since their conceptualisation. However, there is a lack of consensus about the definition, functionality and challenges of Digital Twins. This paper aims to give an overview of what digital twins are, how they are made, the need for a category system to define digital twins and what the greatest challenges are for developing digital twins for CNC machining. This category system is backed with examples from current research of each category and to show the current work on digital twins. Further research has been conducted into what the greatest challenges are for digital twins covering 1258 papers.

articleTitle: A novel technology for monolithic design and manufacturing of off-axis multi-reflection optical system
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Typically, the off-axis multi-reflection optical system is assembled by multiple mirrors, which are designed and machined individually due to the lack of universal mathematical analytic design technology and monolithic manufacturing technology based on a unified benchmark. It will seriously affect the manufacturing quality and overall performance of the optical system. In this paper, a novel method for monolithic design and manufacturing of off-axis multi-reflection optical systems is proposed. An analytical calculation model for automatic quantitative design under manufacturing constraints is established. The single-point diamond turning technology and the adaptive ultra-precision polishing technology with controllable removal are used for monolithic machining. The proposed method has academic value and engineering significance for high precision and efficient design and manufacturing, and optical imaging performance improvement for the off-axis multi-reflection optical system.

articleTitle: Optimal bias voltage of substrate for formable nanocrystalline Niobium precoatings of metallic bipolar plates
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Metallic bipolar plates (BPPs) are key components of the proton exchange membrane fuel cells. To further improve the manufacturing efficiency of metallic BPPs, precoatings have attracted much attention recently. However, precoatings tend to crack and loss the integrity during the forming process. Therefore, formable precoatings are in great demand, and the relationship between deposition and formability of precoatings needs to be studied. In this research, Niobium (Nb) precoatings with different bias voltages of substrate are deposited on SS316L with unbalanced magnetron sputtering process. To evaluate the formability, uniaxial tensile tests are conducted. As the bias voltage increases, the formability of the precoatings firstly increases and reaches the maximum when the bias voltage is −60 V. With further increase of bias voltage, the formability is deteriorated. To understand the effect of bias voltage, the microstructure and surface morphology of the samples are characterized. Nb precoatings with great compactness and nanocrystalline state can sustain 30 % engineering strain when the bias voltage is −60 V, which is the optimal bias voltage for formable Nb precoatings.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis and Digital Design for Non-transferred Plasma Processing
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Direct-current (dc) non-transferred arc plasma torches have been widely used in the processing of metals and related oxides at atmospheric pressure. To optimize the torch structure for better performance on lifetime and thermal efficiency, a 2D axisymmetric, quasi-steady numerical model with multiple phases has been built and validated by the DC torch experiment. The results uncover that the arc inside the torch keeps moving during operation and its start position and moving distance are affected by nozzle length. The predicted peak temperature position on the anode wall by radial current density distribution is in good agreement with temperature distribution on the anode interior surface, which provides clues in the design of torch structure. For thermal efficiency, most power is wasted through a cooled anode wall, whereas a reasonable nozzle length could reduce the energy loss and improve the total input power to achieve better processing ability.

articleTitle: Robust design for the precision forming of metallic bipolar plates of proton exchange membrane fuel cell
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Metallic bipolar plates (BPs) are important components of the proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) which feature large-area dense microchannels. Due to the trans-scale nature of metallic BPs, the frequent local rupture and failure of the microchannels have been a critical problem during the forming process due to the variation of tooling accuracy and material properties. How to design those parameters considering the robustness of the forming process is a key issue to be conquered for the efficient and mass-production of BPs towards PEMFC commercialization. To address that, a detailed discussion was made in this work to find out how the deviations of different processing parameters (r<inf>p</inf>, r<inf>d</inf>, s) and material properties (K, n, ε<inf>0</inf>, and to) affect the thinning behavior in the forming of micro-channels in the bipolar plates. Through actual statistics, finite element simulation, and robust model construction, the influence of the material parameters as well as the characteristic dimensions of the tool on the forming robustness of the bipolar plate was discussed and analyzed. A robust design of the metallic bipolar plate forming process was made by controlling the expectation level and the variance.

articleTitle: The in-mold thermocompression bonding process of microfluidic chips based on the highly dynamic variotherm technology: Process characteristics
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Thermoplastic microfluidic chips show broad development prospects in biomedicine, point-of-care testing, healthcare, and environmental monitoring owing to their advantages in cost, biocompatibility, etc. However, improving the production efficiency of microfluidic chips remains a key industrial challenge to promote the rapid popularization. In this work, we engineered a novel in-mold thermocompression bonding (IMTCB) process based on a highly dynamic mold temperature technology for rapid and mass production of microfluidic chips to overcome the limitations of the traditional thermocompression bonding process in bonding time and process stability. The orthogonal analysis results show that when the bonding strength is taken as the response variable the effect significance of the experimental factors listed from the top is: bonding temperature, bonding pressure, and bonding time. The bond strength increases exponentially with the increasing bonding temperature while increasing linearly with the increasing bonding pressure. The bonding strength can reach around 600 kPa with a microchannel deformation of less than 20%. The bonded thermoplastic microfluidic chips will be manufactured by the IMTCB process from raw materials within 5 minutes.

articleTitle: Study on the effect of HF acid etching on the quality factor and frequency split of fused silica hemispherical resonators
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Nanomanufacturing & 4th AET Symposium on ACSM and Digital Manufacturing (Nanoman-AETS)
abstract: Hemispherical resonator gyroscope is one of the world's most reliable inertial sensors with the longest life span, and has a broad application prospect in aerospace, aviation, vehicles and other navigation fields. The quality factor of hemispherical resonators directly determines the working performance of the hemispherical resonator gyroscope. In this paper, we propose a model to predict the quality factor after grinding by removing subsurface damage of hemispherical resonators by HF etching. We also study the variation law of frequency split of hemispherical resonators in the etching process. The frequency split and quality factor are detected by using frequency sweep and vibration decay methods. The results show that HF etching can raise the quality factor from <tex>$\boldsymbol{5\times 10^{4}}$</tex> to <tex>$\boldsymbol{3\times 10^{6}}$</tex> and the variation pattern verifies the accuracy of the proposed model. The results obtained indicate that the effect of acid etching on the frequency split of the hemispherical resonator is not negligible.
